q1: SELECT b1.name AS bar1, b2.name AS bar2 FROM bar AS b1, bar AS b2 WHERE NOT EXISTS(SELECT s1.beer FROM serves AS s1 WHERE s1.bar = b1.name AND NOT EXISTS(SELECT 1 FROM serves AS s2 WHERE s2.bar = b2.name AND s2.beer = s1.beer)) AND EXISTS(SELECT s2.beer FROM serves AS s2 WHERE s2.bar = b2.name AND NOT EXISTS(SELECT 1 FROM serves AS s1 WHERE s1.bar = b1.name AND s1.beer = s2.beer))
q2: SELECT bar1, bar2 FROM (SELECT s1.bar AS bar1, s2.bar AS bar2, s2.beer FROM serves AS s1 JOIN serves AS s2 ON s1.bar <> s2.bar EXCEPT SELECT s1.bar AS bar1, s2.bar AS bar2, s1.beer FROM serves AS s1 JOIN serves AS s2 ON s1.bar <> s2.bar) AS q

explanation: Q1 and Q2 are not semantically equivalent because they use different approaches to identify bars that serve unique beers (i.e., beers that no other bar serves). The difference in logic can lead to different results, especially when there are multiple bars serving the same beer.
